correctness.rationale: Normalize circumradius to one and set \(p=\pi/n\). The squared radial function is \(\cos^2p\sec^2u\) on a side-normal sector and is \(2p\)-periodic. For odd \(n=2m+1\), a central halfplane's angular interval has length \(m(2p)+p\), so its area equals \(m\) full period integrals plus one length-\(p\) residual. Reducing by dihedral symmetry gives the residual integral \(J(\theta)=\cos^2p[\tan(\theta+p/2)-\tan(\theta-p/2)]\). Dividing by total area yields the stated profile. Its derivative is strictly positive for \(0<\theta<p/2\), and \(J(p/2)=I/2\), proving both uniqueness of the edge-parallel minimum and exact bisection at the symmetry-axis endpoint. The endpoint identity recovers the known depth value. Finite clipping checks are corroborative only.

originality.rationale: Rousseeuw--Ruts already publish the odd regular-polygon maximal-depth value, but in the materially inspected Section 5.5 they explicitly state that the edge-parallel optimizer was verified numerically before computing that value. The new claim gives an exact formula for every central orientation, proves strict monotonicity in a dihedral chamber, and thereby proves and uniquely classifies the optimizer. Targeted published-finding corpus and web searches found no statement implying this profile or uniqueness; the remaining risk is an unindexed or differently phrased later proof.
residual_risks: A later statistics, robust-location, or computational-geometry source may contain an analytic proof of the same orientation profile or optimizer uniqueness under different terminology and may be poorly indexed.
The endpoint maximal-depth value itself is prior work and is intentionally excluded from the novelty claim.

value.rationale: The theorem resolves a specific numerical step explicitly left in the primary regular-polygon depth calculation and strengthens it to a complete directional classification with strict equality information. It is naturally motivated by halfspace depth and Szarek's hyperplane-cut symmetry/floating-body framework. The result is not a recomputation of the known endpoint value: it proves the missing all-order optimizer statement and supplies the entire central orientation profile.
